Remote image processing is explicit, but the external CLI implementation and its claimed safeguards were not available for verification.

content.user_title: Edit Images with GPT Image on RunComfy
content.value_statement: Targeted image edits can change details you want to preserve. This skill provides RunComfy commands and focused prompts for background changes, text replacement, and reference-based composition.
actual_capabilities: Guide requests to the documented openai/gpt-image-2/edit endpoint through the RunComfy CLI.
Structure prompts that specify preserved faces, poses, clothing, branding, and framing before describing changes.
Prepare multilingual headline replacements using exact text, named scripts, and placement instructions.
Compose edits with up to ten reference-image URLs and numbered reference roles.
Configure automatic sizing or three documented fixed output sizes and a local output directory.
Explain authentication prerequisites, CLI exit codes, and when alternative image-editing skills may be more suitable.
limitations: Requires the external RunComfy CLI, an authenticated account, and network access; no CLI implementation is bundled.
Source images must have publicly fetchable HTTPS URLs, and prompts and image references are processed by an external service.
Accepts up to ten image references and only automatic sizing or the three documented fixed sizes.
Complex edits can alter preserved details; the supplied skill includes no executed benchmarks or generated sample assets.

use_cases.title: Localize Advertising Headlines
use_cases.description: Replace embedded headlines with exact translated text while requesting preservation of the photograph, logo, layout, and typography.

use_cases.title: Prepare Product Background Variants
use_cases.description: Request a new studio background while keeping the product, pose, brand mark, and framing unchanged.

use_cases.title: Compose Reference-Based Scenes
use_cases.description: Combine a subject reference with a room reference and specify which image supplies identity, lighting, and color cues.

prompt_templates.title: Replace a Background
prompt_templates.prompt: Use GPT Image Edit on RunComfy with [approved image URL]. Keep the subject, pose, and branding unchanged. Replace only the background with light gray. Preserve the input ratio.
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner: one image and one targeted change.

prompt_templates.title: Replace an Embedded Headline
prompt_templates.prompt: Edit [approved poster URL]. Keep the photograph, logo, layout, and lighting unchanged. Replace only the headline with exactly "[translated text]" in [script]. Retain its position and font weight.

prompt_templates.title: Reposition a Layout Element
prompt_templates.prompt: Edit [approved campaign image URL]. Keep the subject, logo, colors, and headline wording unchanged. Move only the headline from top-right to bottom-center. Use automatic sizing and save to [absolute output directory].
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate: spatial editing with explicit output handling.

prompt_templates.title: Compose Multiple References
prompt_templates.prompt: Use [approved subject URL] as image 1 and [approved room URL] as image 2. Keep image 1 identity, pose, and clothing unchanged. Place that subject in image 2, matching its lighting and palette. Use landscape size 1536_1024 and save to [absolute output directory].
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced: multiple reference roles, preservation constraints, and fixed sizing.

output_examples.input: Replace a portrait background with a light-gray studio backdrop while preserving the person and brand mark.
output: Illustrative result: a portrait with a light-gray studio background and gentle floor shadow.
Review the face, pose, clothing, and brand mark against the original before accepting the edit.
This example describes an expected result, not a generated asset included with the skill.

output_examples.input: Replace only a poster headline with an exact supplied translation while retaining the original layout.
output: Illustrative result: a localized poster with the replacement headline in the requested script, position, and font weight.
Review the spelling, script direction, spacing, and unchanged photograph before publication.
This example describes an expected result, not a verified model output.

best_practices: State what must remain unchanged before requesting one focused edit.
Quote replacement text exactly, name its script, and assign numbered roles to multiple references.
Use only approved image URLs, protect service credentials, and review generated files before publication.
anti_patterns: Combining many unrelated changes in one prompt without explicit preservation requirements.
Paraphrasing replacement headlines or leaving reference-image roles ambiguous.
Submitting confidential images through publicly accessible URLs without authorization for hosting and external processing.

faq.question: What must I install before using this skill?
faq.answer: Install the RunComfy CLI and authenticate with a RunComfy account. The skill provides instructions rather than a bundled image-editing engine.

faq.question: Does image processing happen locally?
faq.answer: No. The documented workflow submits prompts and image references to RunComfy, then downloads generated results into the selected output directory.

faq.question: Can I provide local image paths directly?
faq.answer: The documented images field requires publicly fetchable HTTPS URLs. This skill does not document a local-image upload workflow.

faq.question: How many references and output sizes are supported?
faq.answer: The documented endpoint accepts up to ten reference images. Size choices are auto, 1024_1024, 1024_1536, and 1536_1024.

faq.question: Can it replace text in different languages?
faq.answer: The skill provides multilingual text-editing prompts. Supply exact characters and the script, then review the generated spelling and layout.

faq.question: Does it guarantee unchanged faces and branding?
faq.answer: No. Preservation prompts specify those goals, but complex edits can drift. Compare results with the source before using them.
